# std.spec

Checking observations on small cases: is a table monotone, convex, unimodal or Monge, does a cost satisfy the quadrangle inequality or a split table Knuth's bound, and which recurrence does a sequence follow. Each checker returns the first witness that breaks the law (`None` when it holds), so a brute force over small inputs can print it; the recurrence tools then extend a pinned sequence to any index.

Import: `use std.spec.{...}`.

## Functions

- `fn decrease<T>(xs: List<T>) -> ?Int` — O(n); The first position whose element is below the one before it: `Some(i)` for the smallest `i >= 1` with `xs[i] < xs[i - 1]`, or `None` when `xs` never decreases.
- `fn increase<T>(xs: List<T>) -> ?Int` — O(n); The first position whose element is above the one before it: `Some(i)` for the smallest `i >= 1` with `xs[i] > xs[i - 1]`, or `None` when `xs` never increases.
- `fn convexity_break(xs: List<Int>) -> ?Int` — O(n); The first position where `xs` is not convex: `Some(i)` for the smallest `i` with `xs[i - 1] + xs[i + 1] < 2 * xs[i]`, or `None` when every second difference is at least 0.; traps: never (overflow wraps in release, traps in debug)
- `fn concavity_break(xs: List<Int>) -> ?Int` — O(n); The first position where `xs` is not concave: `Some(i)` for the smallest `i` with `xs[i - 1] + xs[i + 1] > 2 * xs[i]`, or `None` when every second difference is at most 0.; traps: never (overflow wraps in release, traps in debug)
- `fn unimodality_break(xs: List<Int>) -> ?Int` — O(n); The first position where `xs` stops having the shape `ternary_max` needs: strictly rising, then a plateau only at the maximum, then strictly falling.
- `fn monge_break(cost: (Int, Int) -> Int, rows: Int, cols: Int) -> ?(Int, Int)` — O(rows * cols) calls of `cost`; The first 2x2 block of `cost` over `0..rows` by `0..cols` that breaks the Monge law `cost(i, j) + cost(i + 1, j + 1) <= cost(i, j + 1) + cost(i + 1, j)`, as its top-left corner, rows first; `None` when the table is Monge.
- `fn argmins(cost: (Int, Int) -> Int, rows: Int, cols: Int) -> List<Int>` — O(rows * cols) calls of `cost`; The leftmost column of a minimum in each row of `cost` over `0..rows` by `0..cols`, by brute force: the reference that SMAWK, divide and conquer and Knuth's speed-up must reproduce.; traps: when `rows > 0` and `cols < 1`
- `fn dnc_break(cost: (Int, Int) -> Int, n: Int) -> ?(Int, Int)` — O(n^2) calls of `cost`; The first adjacent block of `cost(j, i)` over `0 <= j < i < n` that breaks the quadrangle inequality `cost(a, c) + cost(a + 1, c + 1) <= cost(a, c + 1) + cost(a + 1, c)`, as `(a, c)` with `a + 1 < c`, by `a` then `c`; `None` when it holds (the law `dnc_layer` relies on).
- `fn knuth_break(opt: (Int, Int) -> Int, n: Int) -> ?(Int, Int)` — O(n^2) calls of `opt`; The first interval `[i, j)` of cuts `0..=n` whose best split `opt(i, j)` breaks Knuth's bound `opt(i, j - 1) <= opt(i, j) <= opt(i + 1, j)`, shortest intervals first, then by `i`; `None` when the bound holds (the law `knuth` relies on).
- `fn differences(xs: List<Int>) -> List<Int>` — O(n); The differences of neighbours, `[xs[i + 1] - xs[i] for i in 0..xs.len - 1]`.; traps: never (overflow wraps in release, traps in debug)
- `fn newton(xs: List<Int>) -> List<Int>` — O(n^2); The Newton forward-difference coefficients of `xs`: element `k` is the first entry of the `k`-th differences, so `xs[x] == sum of newton(xs)[k] * choose(x, k)` for every `x` in `0..xs.len`.; traps: never (overflow wraps in release, traps in debug)
- `fn poly_degree(xs: List<Int>) -> ?Int` — O(n^2); The degree of the polynomial `xs` follows at `0, 1, 2, ...`: the smallest `d` whose `(d + 1)`-th differences are all zero, with at least one such difference to confirm it (so `xs.len >= d + 2`); `None` when `xs` is too short to confirm any degree.; traps: never (overflow wraps in release, traps in debug)
- `fn poly_at(xs: List<Int>, n: Int) -> Int` — O(len^2) for `len = xs.len`; The value at `n` of the polynomial of degree below `xs.len` through `(x, xs[x])` for `x` in `0..xs.len`, from its Newton coefficients; `n` may lie outside `0..xs.len` or be negative.; traps: never (overflow wraps in release, traps in debug)
- `fn berlekamp_massey<P>(xs: List<Mod<P>>) -> List<Mod<P>>` — O(n^2) for `n = xs.len`; The shortest linear recurrence `xs` satisfies, by Berlekamp-Massey: `c` with `xs[i] == sum of c[j] * xs[i - 1 - j]` for `j` in `0..c.len`, for every `i >= c.len`.
- `fn recurrence_at<P>(c: List<Mod<P>>, init: List<Mod<P>>, n: Int) -> Mod<P>` — O(k^2 log n) for `k = c.len`; Term `n` of the sequence with recurrence `c` (as `berlekamp_massey` returns it) and first terms `init`: `init[n]` for `n < c.len`, else by Kitamasa, `x^n` modulo the characteristic polynomial.; traps: when `n < 0` or `init.len != c.len`
- `fn guess_at<P>(xs: List<Mod<P>>, n: Int) -> ?Mod<P>` — O(xs.len^2 + k^2 log n) for the recurrence length `k`; Term `n` of `xs` extended by the shortest recurrence it satisfies, or `None` when `xs` is too short to pin that recurrence: Berlekamp-Massey finds `c`, and the guess stands only when `xs.len > 2 * c.len`, so at least one term past the ones that determine `c` agrees with it.; traps: when `n < 0`
